summary: "Cancionero de Lope de Stúñiga: Códice del siglo XV" by Fuensanta del Valle et al. is a poetry collection compiled between 1460 and 1463. This cancionero preserves lyric poetry from the court of Alfonso V of Aragón in Naples, where Castilian and Aragonese poets flourished under Italian Quattrocento influence. Named after Lope de Stúñiga, whose work opens the collection, it features verses from numerous court poets and notably includes some romances, distinguishing it among fifteenth-century Spanish literary anthologies.
